cards.explanation: The answer is Canaanite. Judah, one of Jacob's sons (Genesis 35:23), leaves his brothers and settles near Hirah, an Adullamite. There he sees the daughter of a Canaanite man named Shua and takes her as his wife (Genesis 38:2). Friends, that verse moves faster than I do when the oven timer goes off.

The word is wicked. The text says Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD, so the LORD put him to death. It doesn't say what Er did, so I won't guess. I think this one is heavy, friends, and it's okay to feel that.

The offspring is for his brother Er. Judah tells Onan, his second son, to perform his duty as her brother-in-law and raise up offspring for his brother (Genesis 38:8). So the offspring would be Er's. Onan was handed a job for somebody else's name, and it's right there in Genesis 38:8.
The answer is True. What Onan did was wicked in the sight of the LORD, so He put Onan to death as well. That's two brothers now. I'll just say it plainly, friends: this part is heavy.

Judah tells her to live as a widow in her father's house. He says, “Live as a widow in your father’s house until my son Shelah grows up.” (Genesis 38:11) So Tamar packs up and goes. Judah's youngest was the one she was waiting on.

The answer is False. The text says Judah thought, “He may die too, like his brothers.” (Genesis 38:11) That thought comes with his words to Tamar: live as a widow in her father's house until Shelah grows up. I think that's a worried thought.
The word is shear. Somebody tells Tamar that Judah is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep. Verse 12 says he's going to his sheepshearers there. Tamar gets the news, and she's listening.

The answer is False. Verse 14 says Shelah had grown up, yet Tamar had not been given to him as a wife. Earlier, Judah told her to live as a widow until Shelah grew up (Genesis 38:11). Shelah has grown, and she has not been given to him. That's what Tamar sees.
The word is veil. Tamar removes her widow's garments and covers her face with a veil to disguise herself. Then she sits where Judah will pass. A plan is in motion, friends.

He takes her for a prostitute. The text says when Judah saw her, he thought she was a prostitute because she had covered her face. He didn't realize who she was. The disguise worked, and it's all in verse 15.
The word is goat, a young goat. Judah says, “I will send you a young goat from my flock…” (Genesis 38:17) He's promising to pay later. A promise alone is hard to hold, friends.

She asks for his seal and cord and staff. Tamar answers, “Your seal and your cord, and the staff in your hand.” (Genesis 38:18) Judah hands them over, and she becomes pregnant by him. Remember those three items, friends, because they matter later.
The answer is True. Judah sends Hirah with the young goat, and Hirah could not find her. Verse 20 says he went to collect the items Judah had left with the woman. He's got the goat, and she's gone.

The men tell him, “No shrine prostitute has been here…” (Genesis 38:21) That's the whole answer. I bet Hirah wished for a different one, because who wants to carry that news back? He does it anyway, and in verse 22 he tells Judah, “I could not find her…”

His reason is that they won't become a laughingstock. Judah says, “Let her keep the items. Otherwise we will become a laughingstock.” (Genesis 38:23) He lets his seal, cord and staff go rather than keep asking around. Nothing else is given as the reason.

Judah orders that she be burned to death. He says, “Bring her out! Let her be burned to death!” (Genesis 38:24) I think this one hurts to read, friends. Hold on, because the story isn't done with this moment.

Her message says she's pregnant by the owner of these items. Tamar sends word, “I am pregnant by the man to whom these items belong.” (Genesis 38:25) She doesn't name him. She lets the items do the talking.

The word is righteous. Judah says, “She is more righteous than I, since I did not give her to my son Shelah.” (Genesis 38:26) He names what he did not do. Friends, I'd say owning a mistake out loud is a good example for all of us.

The answer is True. Genesis 38:27 says that when the time came for Tamar to give birth, there were twins in her womb. Twins would mean double the cookie cutters for me, and I'd lose count by the second one. And the next verses have a hand in them.
The answer is wrist. The midwife takes a scarlet thread and ties it around his wrist. Then she announces which one came out first. A little bright thread on a very small arm.

The answer is False. The baby pulled his hand back and his brother came out (Genesis 38:29). Then his brother came out with the scarlet thread around his wrist (Genesis 38:30). So the twin with the thread was born second. He stuck his hand out first and still lost the race, and that's a rough day at the starting line.

The name is Perez. The midwife says, “You have broken out first!” and the text says, “So he was named Perez.” (Genesis 38:29) His brother, with the scarlet thread, is Zerah. The name matches what happened.
